stem.en: A researcher identifies a unicellular eukaryote as a fungus. Which features would support keeping it in Kingdom Fungi?

text.en: A cell wall of cellulose, and food made using sunlight.

feedback.en: Those are features of plants and some protists. A fungus makes no food, and its wall is chitin.

text.en: No true nucleus, and food absorbed from around it.

feedback.en: No true nucleus would place it in Monera. This organism is a eukaryote, so it has a true nucleus.

text.en: A chitin wall, and food absorbed from around it.

feedback.en: Yes. Yeast stays in Fungi for these two reasons, although it has only one cell.

text.en: No cell wall at all, and many cilia for moving.

feedback.en: Those features fit a protist such as Paramecium, not a fungus.

explanation.en: One cell does not rule out Fungi. Yeast is unicellular, but its chitin wall and its way of absorbing food place it with moulds and mushrooms.

hints.en: Think about what yeast shares with a mushroom.
